Your own guild, right on your desktop!

All Peaceful at the Adventurer's Guild Today is an idle RPG designed to sit neatly on the side of your desktop.

Become the Guild Master, recruit adventurers, grow your characters, and collect and upgrade equipment. Your adventurers will fight on their own, bringing back various rewards and resources.

Explore Dungeons Whenever You Have Time

Click the Guild Receptionist to check for new missions.

Recruit a Variety of Adventurers at the Tavern

Use the resources you earn to make your adventurers stronger, challenge new areas and more powerful enemies, and continue growing your guild.

The game can be displayed in a small window on the side of your desktop. Watch your adventurers fight and grow while working or doing other things, then return to the game whenever you're ready to start your next adventure.

One button. Zero margin for error. Humanity's last hope.Alpha 7: The Last Hope is an extreme-precision, high-speed space arcade game where you pilot your ship with a single key. Dodge millimeter-accurate asteroid choreographies, manage your reactor's temperature on the razor's edge, and survive anomalies that warp gravity and the very reality of your screen.

[YOUR MECHANICS BANNER / HEAT & ANOMALIES SYSTEM GIF GOES HERE]

Survive the Cosmic Chaos

  • One-Key Control, Tactical Depth: Easy to grasp in a second, brutal to master. Thrust your ship at the exact right millisecond to thread through impossible corridors.

  • Deterministic Choreographies: Forget luck. Every level follows an exact spatial sequence based on distance traveled—learn the rhythm, memorize the patterns, and master the void.

  • Critical Reactor Management: Your ship constantly builds up heat. Collect ice fragments before core temperature hits 100% and triggers a meltdown.

  • EMP Aliens & Visual Anomalies: Face enemies that invert your gravity and spatial distortions that flip your camera upside down, mirror your controls, or alter the color spectrum mid-run.

  • Vaporization & Quantum Shields: Gather blue fragments to regenerate shields, or trigger invincibility to pulverize asteroids in your path for massive bonus points.

12 Ships with Unique Abilities & Routes

Unlock a fleet of 12 spacecraft, each featuring distinct stats, passive abilities, and exclusive obstacle sequences:

  • Pilot everything from Dave's versatile main ship to specialized units like Angel-18 (immune to gravity inversion), Z-Kelvin (advanced thermal cooling), Midas Rich (2x score multiplier), or Phoenix Infinity.

  • Switching ships doesn't just change your durability or speed—it completely alters the formation patterns you'll face in every level.

Game Modes, Competitive ELO & the "Evil Panel"

  • Simulation System: Sharpen your reflexes and learn the core mechanics in a controlled training environment.

  • Galactic Legend: Conquer the main campaign across 5 intense sectors featuring dialogues, cinematic events, and an epic climax.

  • Space Survival & Secret Level: Test your endurance in a pure survival mode that leads into a secret stage built to push your reflexes to the absolute limit.

  • Scalable Difficulty: Play on Normal, take on classic arcade punishment in Hard, activate the extreme modifiers of the Evil Panel (+50% speed, +50% duration, or both), or race against an endless clock in Last Breath.

  • ELO Ranking System: Measure your true skill level with a competitive algorithm that evaluates your win rate, precision, shields earned, and high score.

Expanded Universe & Multilingual Voice Acting

  • 21-Chapter Lore Book: Unlock and read the full story behind the Alpha 7 mission as you progress and overcome challenges.

  • Voice Acting in 5 Languages: Immerse yourself in the action with dialogues and combat alerts recorded in English, Japanese, Mandarin, Russian, and German.

AmaTisMo is an inclusive visual novel about mental health, depression, and self-love.

You play as Amatista, a young woman trapped in depressive isolation. When an unexpected event forces her out of her apartment, she begins a journey she never asked for, one that will challenge everything she believes about herself and the world around her.

Every dialogue choice feeds into a branching story system. The game tracks your decisions, big and small, and characters react accordingly. The path through Amatista's story is yours to define, and there is no single right answer.

3 acts. 10 chapters. 5 endings.

Built from the ground up to be fully accessible for blind and visually impaired players, with complete screen reader support, keyboard navigation, and audio descriptions.

Amateur Football Together is a 5v5 cage football game about the best part of the week: the after-work match with your mates. Everyone controls one player, bots and AI goalkeepers fill the gaps, and the ball never leaves the cage.

Jump into a room, pick your kit, and play fast, scrappy, physical football under the sunset lights of a seaside city. Nobody is a pro here. The passes go astray, the keeper has one good save in him, and someone always shouts for the ball when they're completely marked.

One player, one body

You control a single footballer from a third-person view behind your player. Aim with the mouse, hold to power your shot and release to strike. Every touch is yours: first-time volleys, chest control, headers, close-control dribbling, knock-ons into space and last-ditch slide tackles.

Football that feels good

  • Ground passes, lofted passes, through balls and crosses, all aimed where you're looking

  • Placed finishes, driven shots and chips with real ball physics, spin and bounce

  • Two dribbling modes: tight close control under pressure, or knock the ball ahead and sprint

  • Shoulder-to-shoulder contact: step into a dribbler's path and knock the ball loose

  • Stamina and sprinting, so you have to pick your moments

Drop in, play, drop out

  • Up to 8 players: 4 outfield players plus an AI goalkeeper per team

  • Bots take over any empty or abandoned spot, so every match is always 5v5

  • Short matches: two 4-minute halves, no offsides, no throw-ins, no stoppages

  • Practice against bots offline at your own pace

Talk without typing

Hit 1, 2, 3 or 4 for quick-chat calls and emoji reactions. Ask for the ball, cheer a worldie, or wind up the other team, all without leaving the pitch.

Make it yours

Choose your footballer, pick a kit design and your shirt number. Your look is synced to everyone in the room.

Sunset cage

A floodlit rooftop-style cage pitch with neon hotels on one side and the ocean on the other, confetti on every goal, and a crowd of mates who will never let you forget that miss.

Keyboard and mouse recommended. Xbox and PlayStation controllers are supported for gameplay and menus.

DESTROY THE SOURCE

The monsters just keep coming.

Fight your way through relentless hordes, hunt down the Spawners summoning endless enemies, and tear them apart before they overwhelm you. If luck isn't on your side, skill will have to be.

BET ON YOUR BUILD

The best runs aren't built by chance alone.

Choose your starting items, complete objectives, and maximize your growth before the boss appears. Every decision could be the one that changes everything if luck is on your side.

MAKE EVERY SPIN COUNT

When the moment is right, spin the Legendary Slot Machine.

Hit the jackpot to become 18× stronger. Choose when to gamble. Play it safe, or bet big. The right spin can make all the difference.

HIT THE COMBAT JACKPOT

Swords, Guns... God Finger?

Select your player with their own combat specialty and unlock weapons to mow down the hordes. Luck will help, but your skill will unlock unique weapons. Master them all.

EVEN DEATH IS A GAMBLE

It's never really over until you lose it all.

Spin the Legendary Slot Machine. Revive or die. Feeling lucky?

EXPECT THE UNEXPECTED

Think you've figured the game out?

Bonus Stages play by completely different rules. Adapt, improvise, and discover new ways to survive.

Build a village worth defending. Turn a small settlement into a thriving home, grow its economy, and raise a force that can hold the line against waves of fantasy monsters. Village building, resource management, and automatic battles meet in a cycle of growth, defense, and rebuilding.

Grow your village

Start with simple homes and production buildings, then expand as your resources allow. Farms, foresters, and quarries supply your growing settlement. Decide how much to invest in the economy and how much to commit to defense before the next threat arrives.

Build your defenders

Develop your military buildings and bring together warriors, archers, and magic users. Watch your forces fight along the village walls as enemy waves test the strength of your settlement. From small creatures to towering foes, each fight puts your preparations to work.

Rebuild stronger

A fallen village is another chance to improve. Spend earned Skulls on persistent upgrades across Prosperity, Valor, and Sorcery, strengthening your economy, fighters, and magic for the next village. Try a different balance of growth and defense and see how much further you can go.

Features

  • Village building: Expand housing, resource production, and military buildings.

  • Resource management: Balance your settlement's needs with the cost of a stronger defense.

  • Automatic battles: Build your forces and watch them face incoming monster waves.

  • Warriors, archers, and magic: Develop different defenders as your village grows.

  • Lasting progression: Use Skulls to invest in Prosperity, Valor, and Sorcery between villages.

  • Medieval fantasy presentation: Detailed village buildings and side-view battles against fantastical enemies.

Dahlonega, Georgia. 1829.

The gold is down there. The ground will not tell you where.

Swing a pick into Georgia red clay and find out what you struck. Sometimes it is nothing, forty times in a row. Sometimes the shovel turns over something that stops you where you stand.

Go deeper for the good stuff. Deeper is also where the ground starts fighting back.

Follow a hunch sideways and you might hit a run of ore that goes on and on. Or you might chase it half a day and get eleven dollars for your trouble. That is prospecting. You do not find out until you dig.

Haul it up, sell it before the assayer shuts, and start buying the town, one business at a time. Ruby runs the saloon, and she is always where the party is at during the night.  But don't stay up too late, you have to hit the mine early!

The Fun

  • Dig, strike, and find out what you struck

  • Every swing is a guess you paid for

  • Chase a seam across the hill and hope it holds

  • Go deep for the good stuff, and see what is waiting down there

  • Blow a hole with some dynamite!  But look out, who knows how long it's been sitting. 

Own every business in town, or die of exhaustion trying

CATS, FISH, AND SUSPICION

Among Paws is a cozy 4–8 player social deduction party game where sneaky cats steal fish at night, accuse each other in the morning, and race to become the first 5 kg champion.


Every night, one or more cats wake up with a secret plan: steal the fish without getting caught.

Steal the fish carefully. The other cats may be sleeping, but every suspicious move can come back to haunt you in the morning.

HOW IT PLAYS

When morning comes, everyone gathers around the table to discuss, bluff, defend, and accuse.

Choose carefully.

Accuse the real thief, and the innocent cats share the fish.

Accuse the wrong cat, and the thief enjoys the feast.

Discuss in the morning
Innocent cats search for clues while thieves bluff their way out.

Vote for the suspect
The table decides which cat looks the most suspicious.

STEAL, BLUFF, ACCUSE

Steal the fish at night
Sneaky cats make their move while the others sleep.

Bluff your way out
If you are the thief, stay calm, act innocent, and convince everyone to blame another cat.

Catch the real thief
If you are innocent, listen carefully, watch the table, and vote before the thief gets away.

Every round is short, social, and chaotic. One clever lie or one perfect accusation can change who gets the fish.

RACE TO 5 KG

Every successful round makes the winning cats heavier.

Winners eat the fish, grow bigger, and get closer to victory.

The first cat to reach 5 kg wins the game.

No eliminations, no waiting
Every cat stays in the game, and every round matters.

Even if you lose a vote, you are never removed from the match. You keep playing, keep accusing, and keep fighting for the next fish.

WHY PLAY AMONG PAWS?

A colorful twist on social deduction

Fast rounds built for friend groups

Cute cats, suspicious behavior, and chaotic accusations

A race-to-5 kg victory goal instead of player elimination

Voice and text chat support for bluffing, arguing, and meowing your way to victory

The city has a zombie problem.

Quite a big one.

Pick a district, get in there, and deal with AN UNREASONABLE NUMBER OF ZOMBIES.

Kill zombies. Earn coins. Buy guns. Barricade doors. Try not to get eaten.

But that's only half the problem.

Every run is a gamble.

The longer you stay, the more you can earn... and the worse things get.

Secure what you've got, or push your luck for more. Yoinks!

Every district is a different fight.

New layouts.

New objectives.

New problems.

What worked last time might not work here.

The infection doesn't stop while you're busy somewhere else.

Choose where you fight. The places you leave behind get worse.

COINS keep you going during a run. Spend them on guns, repairs and whatever else you need.

LOOT makes you stronger for the next one.

What you do in one run changes what comes next.

Districts you've fought for, places you've neglected, and an infection that keeps spreading- it's all still there when you come back. Oh joy!

Bash 'em. Beat 'em. Shoot 'em. Repeat.

When the city throws an unreasonable number of zombies at you, you gotta do what you gotta do.

FEATURES

  • Each district has different rules and win conditions

  • A push-your-luck gamble at the end of every stage (3 waves)

  • Chunky voxel zombies with dismemberment and blood,..oh so much blood

  • A city that changes based on where you went and where you didn't

  • Permanent perks you keep for good - Woo-hoo!

  • COINS off dead zombies for guns, walls, and patch-ups

  • Single-player and fully offline

  • Coming at launch: Steam Cloud saves, full Steam Input support, and Remote Play on your TV

  • Did I mention that the game has AN UNREASONABLE NUMBER OF ZOMBIES?!

China's invasion of Taiwan has only just begun, and the air raids have reached Tainan. Taiwan's air defenses stopped most of what came in, but parts of Anping, a district of the city, were still hit. To be safe, the local government evacuated everyone who lived there.

The evacuation notice came through on your phone. You stayed put.

Not because you're brave. You've never cared much about what goes on around you. You don't follow the news, you don't do politics, and you don't go out if you can help it. Packing a bag, queuing, squeezing onto a bus with a crowd of strangers: just thinking about it is exhausting. You stayed for one reason only. You're lazy, the same way you're too lazy to care about anything else.

The trouble is, you're a homebody through and through, and you've got no idea how to survive. You hardly ever go out, so you couldn't even say what the streets around your own building look like. Cooking's out of the question. All you can count on is food you can eat as it is: canned food and emergency rations.

Next morning you open your eyes and you're still alive. Outside the window everything is chaos. The power is out, and whatever was in the fridge has probably turned.

That's where the game starts.

There's no base to defend and no fighting your way out. What you have to do is far more ordinary: stay alive one more day, in an apartment with no electricity, on whatever you can turn up by going through drawers.

This isn't a game about a hero. It's a game about the person who didn't leave: why they didn't, whether they still could, and how to get through the next few hours.

Only a few cards in front of you

Along the bottom of the screen sit a handful of action cards, and they change with where you are. The bedroom lets you sleep, the kitchen lets you go through the cupboards, the temple lets you cast the moon blocks. All you do is decide what the next stretch of time gets spent on.

Status, Resources, Quests and Notes, top left, are for looking. Pressing them costs no time.

  • Search: go through the room. There are cans in the kitchen cupboard, but you'll need to find the can opener first. Until then a can is just a sealed tin.

  • Move: walking from the bedroom to the bathroom takes a few minutes. Taking the stairs down from the tenth floor is another matter entirely. The lift doesn't work. There's no power.

  • Eat, drink, sleep: a salty can will leave you thirstier. Sleeping saves your game, and puts you through a whole night at your most vulnerable.

Every action card spends in-game time, and how much it spends is decided by the thing itself. Opening one drawer and descending ten flights of stairs are not the same errand. An older body takes longer over the same walk than a young one, and longer still when it can barely stand.

Time is the only genuinely scarce thing here. Your body will not wait for you.

What you're up against isn't a who. It's eight numbers going down

Health, fullness, thirst, energy, body temperature, injury, mood, hygiene. Each falls at its own pace, and none of them is a case of "higher is better": eating until you're stuffed is as much a problem as passing out from hunger. Every one of them has a comfortable range.

The weather won't cooperate either. Full four-season simulation: the gap between day and night temperatures, rain that settles in for days, a typhoon that arrives without warning. Nobody gets to predict tomorrow. Whatever you wake up to is the weather you get. When it rains, it really rains out there, and the drops run down the lens.

When it's cold, a down jacket is worth far more than a can of pineapple.

Taiwanese

Taiwanese is a language a great many people in Taiwan speak every day. Speaking it takes no thought. Writing it down or reading it is where most people get stuck. There was a generation that was fined and made to wear a sign for speaking Taiwanese at school, and what survived that was the speaking, and only the speaking.

This game's dialogue is written in Taiwanese Pe̍h-ōe-jī (POJ), a romanised orthography. Choose Taiwanese and you can pick a second language to run alongside it: POJ on top, the one you can read underneath. If you speak it but can't read it, you can match the sounds up as you play. If you don't speak it at all, you still know what you're reading.

Supported languages: Taiwanese Mandarin, Taiwanese (Pe̍h-ōe-jī), English, Japanese and German.

You decide who you are in the opening minutes

At the moment you wash your face and look in the bathroom mirror: young / adult / older, male / female, six combinations. Different bodies start in different places.

You get stronger after that. Carrying things, walking a long way, forcing yourself to stay awake: anything you do might build up some part of you a little. Get stronger and you can carry more. Build stamina and the same job tires you less.

Who you turn into depends on what you have actually done these last few days.

What you can carry, and what you can't

Supplies have weight, and you have two hands, one backpack, and perhaps a cart. What to take and what to leave behind is a trade-off you are forced into at every turn.

An expired packet of curry is both a liquid food and an expired item. Whether you eat it is your call.

That raincoat won't make you warm. What it guarantees is that you won't get soaked through. And being soaked makes your body temperature fall much faster.

Step outside and things happen

Go somewhere and a chance card sometimes turns up. There's more than one kind, and you won't know which until it's turned over. When your luck is bad, it's a robber.

Run, hide or fight: that's your call. Fight, and you sit down at a card table. Your deck is your body: your strength, your fighting, whether you've eaten. The bat in your hand becomes a card too, and the more you use it, the sooner it breaks. The cards come in three kinds: Strike beats Grab, Grab beats Guard, Guard beats Strike. Both sides turn theirs over at once.

If you'd rather not sit through it, you can just get it over with in a single roll.

Lose, and you get hurt, and what you're carrying may be taken. Win, and their supplies are yours, and now and then they drop a piece of gear with an extra bonus. Some things only robbers carry.

Luckier people run into robbers less often, and the ones they do meet are hungrier.

Moon blocks

Heng-hô Temple is still standing. There's nobody inside, but the moon blocks are still on the altar.

Carry a peace charm and some joss paper, and you can cast the blocks there, asking the god to bless the charm. It takes three siūⁿ-poe in a row: a yes, a yes, a yes. A single laughing pair or a single no means the god has said no this time, and that charm can't ask again today. After the third yes you burn the joss paper, and only then is it done. Where the blessing lands and how much it gives is up to the god.

A charm from another temple works too. It's just harder.

There is nobody to ask

There are no NPCs in this game. From beginning to end, the only voice you hear is the protagonist talking to themself.

Hidden in the rooms are note fragments, and the only way to turn one up is to search. They tell how this war got to where it is: the announcements, the notices, the days that were once entirely unremarkable. Every place you've been stays in your notes too, one instant photo at a time.

None of it affects whether you survive. You can go a whole playthrough without finding a single one and still get through every day.

But you will not meet anyone you can actually talk to in this game, and the fragments are the only way you'll come to know any of them. Whether the protagonist stops to finish reading is itself part of who they are.

About the name

Anping is a district of Tainan, and the place where this story happens.

Read its two characters the other way round and you get 平安: safe, unharmed, having come through it. A place name that also happens to be a wish.

An-pêng, set alongside the title, is how those two characters sound in Taiwanese, written in Pe̍h-ōe-jī. It isn't Mandarin romanisation. In Mandarin the same place is Anping.

About the artwork

Every scene starts as a photograph taken on location in Anping. The photo is processed first: things that shouldn't be in the frame and anything touching on someone's privacy come out, and real shop names and signs are swapped for made-up ones, so the FamilyMart on the corner is EasyMart in the game. Then AI turns it into an animated style.

The interface is being redesigned too. The frames on the buttons and panels are drawn from old Taiwanese window lattices and from the bastions that jut out at the four corners of An-pêng Old Fort and Ek-chài Fortress. The scene name plates also borrow the iron wall anchors on Anping's old houses.

Reporting a problem

If the game runs into an error, or didn't close normally last time, you can send a report to the developer from inside the game. No need to go looking for files.

Nothing is sent until you press Send Report. What gets sent is what you wrote, the game version and your system (models such as your operating system and graphics card), the game's logs and screen pictures, and your save if you tick the box. Your user name is removed from file paths first.

All of it is used only to find and fix problems. The full details are in the privacy policy linked on this store page.

Where development stands

This is a project in development, currently made by one person.

The core systems are running: time, weather, status resolution, supplies, story, quests, chance cards and the card table are all in place. You can already get out of the building: the courtyard, the lane, and nine places in the streets around it. Early Access will keep going further out, with all of Anping as the goal.

The interface is gradually being replaced with its own design: Status, Resources, Quests and Notes are notebooks, dialogue boxes and the settings are written on paper, and the dark buttons and panels are framed with bastion corners. That work carries on through Early Access.

Play with keyboard and mouse or with a controller, and rebind any key you like.

Early Access launches on 10 December 2026 (9 December in the Americas).

Ancient Duel is a historical tactical card game built around short, strategic 1v1 battles between the great civilizations of the ancient world.

Build a 40-card deck, choose your factions, deploy units and commanders, and use doctrines, tactics and terrain to control the battlefield. Every turn is a contest of positioning, timing and resource management — knowing when to attack can matter just as much as knowing which card to play.

Build Your Strategy

Create decks around Rome, Egypt, Persia, Sparta, Macedonia, Carthage and Dacia, each with its own battlefield identity and tactical strengths.

Combine cards and factions to create different approaches to battle, from disciplined defensive formations and ranged pressure to cavalry maneuvers, ambushes and aggressive assaults.

Fight for Position

Ancient Duel is not only about the cards in your hand.

Units occupy battlefield positions, attacks are directed across opposing lines, and defensive support can change the outcome of combat. Commanders, doctrines, tactics and terrain create additional layers of interaction, making positioning and sequencing central to every match.

Manage Your Resources

Energy determines what you can deploy and activate. Strong turns require planning ahead rather than simply playing the most powerful card available.

Build pressure, protect important units, anticipate your opponent and decide when to commit your resources.

History Turned Into Gameplay

Cards are inspired by real historical units, commanders, military doctrines and battlefield tactics.

Legionaries, phalanxes, cavalry, war elephants, archers and famous commanders are translated into gameplay mechanics designed to reflect the character of their civilizations while keeping battles accessible and competitive.

Key Features

  • Tactical 1v1 turn-based card battles

  • 7 ancient factions with distinct strategic identities

  • 40-card deckbuilding

  • Multi-faction deck combinations

  • Battlefield positioning and formation-based combat

  • Units, commanders, doctrines, tactics and terrain

  • Historically inspired cards and mechanics

  • Free-to-play competitive strategy

What's in the Demo

The demo is the full game with the competitive economy switched off — nothing is time-limited and nothing is locked behind a paywall:

  • All 7 factions — Rome, Sparta, Macedonia, Carthage, Persia, Dacia and Egypt — and all 141 cards

  • The whole campaign: 7 campaigns, 35 missions, 19 historical battles and 42 achievements

  • Tutorial and practice matches against the AI

  • Ranked and Private online duels — Steam matches demo players with other demo players

  • Local play over the same Wi-Fi, with no server in between

  • Full controller support and native Windows, macOS, Linux and Steam Deck builds

Your campaign progress and achievements are saved on your device.

Planned for the Full Release

The full release of Ancient Duel is planned to expand the experience with:

  • Organized tournaments — Arena Trials, Grand Conquest and weekend events

  • Championship Points — a seasonal competitive ladder

  • Progression and reward systems — Credits earned in play and alternative decks to unlock

  • Print & Play content

  • Steam achievements and cloud saves

More features and content will be revealed as development continues. The full game is free to play — add Ancient Duel to your wishlist to be told when it launches.

Andrea Shattered Two Hundred Years Ago

They call it the Severance. Three primal forces tore loose from the collapsing leylines and warped the land, its creatures, and everyone left standing.

Survivors have lasted this long on Runes dug out of the rubble — fragments of power frozen at the instant of the Severance, each one holding somebody's obsession, or the memory of some place.

But the Severance never ended. It is still spreading.

You are a Traveler. Your job is to walk toward its source, find out what lies underneath — and put a stop to it.

How far you get depends on the decisions you can't take back.

What Drops Is Fine. What You Build Is Yours.

Gear still falls off enemies. You just don't get a say in what rolls on it.

Elites and Area Bosses leave Blueprints — a piece of gear before it has a shape. Fit material Tiles onto the crafting board; every placement buys you Malleability, and you spend it deciding which Affixes go in and which ones get pushed further.

The Tiles come off a shuffled deck. The board is different every time. The same Blueprint can become two completely different weapons.

You're not waiting on luck. You're negotiating with it.

You Will Never Walk the Whole Map

The dungeon unfolds under fog, and it always offers more paths than you have time for.

Every fight, every crafting stop, every visit to the shop burns time you can't get back. And the longer you take, the stronger the things ahead of you become.

Detour to uncover what's out there, or go straight for the Area Boss? Stop and finish that weapon, or push on while you can still win fights?

When the time runs out, the map closes in — and there's only one path left, between you and whatever is waiting at the end of it.

The Same Tree Never Grows Twice

Every character has their own Talent tree, and that tree regrows every run.

Some nodes are still blank when you reach them. This run they hand you critical strikes and life steal; the next they might grow poison and spread. Even the Capstone at the far end is no exception.

Your points only cover a fraction of it. Sigils come in four colors, and whichever ones you pick up along the way decide which core nodes will open for you. Try to have everything and you'll reach none of it.

And there's no respec. Every step counts.

Nobody Is Born a Traveler

They came out of the forges of the Iron Curtain Workshop, the corridors of the Silent Academy, the songs of the Windsong Plains — each of them left the place they came from, and none of them will say why.

Now they walk the same road: into the deepest warped ground, and back out again if they can.

Each one brings their own Talent tree, their own Runes, their own way to fight.

Clearing It Is Not the End

Win once and the Andrea Cycle turns to the next page.

The rules get rewritten: costs climb, enemies get meaner, and some thresholds stop being optional. Every character tracks how deep into the Cycle they've made it, on their own.

You think you have this continent figured out. The Cycle disagrees.

Andromeda Wars is a retro‑styled space RTS built for massive fleet battles, fast decision‑making, and high‑pressure resource management. Gather power, expand your forces, fortify your mothership, and survive the relentless assault of rival factions. Every ship you deploy strengthens your fleet but drains your limited power, forcing you to balance aggression, defence, and long‑term survival.

Command huge battles across handcrafted missions, skirmish maps, and fully custom scenarios. Use the built‑in map editor to create your own battlefields and share them with the community through Steam Workshop.

A unique time‑slow mechanic gives you tactical clarity: selecting a unit slows the battlefield, letting you line up attacks, prioritise targets, and execute precise manoeuvres even in the chaos of large‑scale combat.

Features

  • Large‑scale battles designed for explosive fleet‑on‑fleet combat.

  • 13 unique units, each offering different tactical advantages.

  • 20 campaign missions plus additional skirmish maps.

  • 6 distinct game modes that dramatically change how you gather and spend power.

  • Time‑slow targeting for precise control in the heat of battle.

  • Full map editor to build your own maps.

  • Steam Workshop support for sharing and downloading custom maps.

Game Modes

  • Normal — Limited power for fast, focused matches.

  • Unlimited — Infinite power for huge, chaotic battles.

  • Domination — Start with fixed power; earn more by destroying enemies. Defensive units disabled.

  • Switch — Power sources teleport around the map, forcing constant repositioning.

  • On the Go — Power sources drift across the battlefield, pushing players into conflict.

  • Power Burst — Everyone receives equal power in timed bursts, making skill the deciding factor.

Angel Guardian is a sci-fi side-scrolling action shooter built around fast combat, smart movement, and constant pressure.

After a sudden attack cripples the Space Station kingdom of Alterra, its systems turn against you — and survival becomes the mission.

Survive using multiple tools and playstyles:

  • Tight, fast-paced shooting built for constant movement.

  • Collect 8 double-upgradeable rifles plus a sword.

  • Stealth options to avoid combat or strike quietly.

  • Hacking systems to disable defenses, crack codes, and gain access to hidden areas.

  • Deadly enemies and boss encounters that demand quick reactions.

Angel Guardian features Twitch Chat Integration that lets viewers affect the game in real time:

  • Spawn enemies right in your path.

  • Drop ammo when you’re desperate.

  • Trigger Eiji’s superpowers.

Every run becomes unpredictable —share the IDs with your chat and let them unleash mayhem live while you fight to survive.

You play as Kita, a warrior guardian sent to extract a young prince after the attack.

As the journey unfolds, the prince fights alongside you, unlocking powerful abilities while you help him awaken his true potential as the kingdom’s rightful heir.

This is not an escort mission. This is a fight to take control back.

Tested by 100+ players across multiple closed test sessions.

Wishlist now to stay updated and not miss the launch. See you out there, Guardian!

Animal Clicking is a relaxing genre-mashup. It takes the cozy vibe of an island builder and fuses it with the addictive "one more thing" loop of a clicker game—all set on a vibrant, customizable island.

Start with a simple wheat field, get your first workers to help you with the clicking, and send the rocket to the motherland to unlock ever more ways to increase the harvest.

Decorate and customize your island to your heart’s desire and create a beautiful haven of glorious labor and high-yield production.

Every great harvest begins with a single click. Take direct control of your island's destiny by tending to your fields manually to jumpstart your production. Feel the progress as you click to make your crops sprout and flourish.

In this world, your effort translates directly into growth, turning tiny sprouts into a blooming fortune.

The land is free, and the possibilities endless. Lay down sprawling crop fields or cozy animal pens to diversify your resources. Upgrade your buildings to unlock higher yields, increased capacity, and more efficient production.

From a simple farm to a sophisticated agricultural hub, every upgrade brings you closer to perfecting your output.

Labor is cheap and plentiful. Recruit a cast of adorable, hardworking animals to do the dirty work for you. Use intuitive drag-and-drop mechanics to assign your workers exactly where they are needed most. Watch as your island comes to life, with your loyal workers growing, harvesting, and storing—because they definitely love it.

Strategically place your workers at their preferred workplace to maximize output and keep your production flowing at rocket speed. As you unlock more help, you’ll shift from manual clicking to managing and overseeing your ever-expanding workforce. But be careful: overworking your furry workforce might lead to exhaustion and slower production.

The Motherland awaits your resources. Send your produce to the stars and unlock new possibilities. The rocket is always ready for your next delivery of fresh crops, produce, or gold.

Load the rocket, launch it, and accelerate your progress. New crops, buildings, and decorations wait for you to be unlocked.

No two islands look the same! Experience a relaxing yet addictive progression system that rewards you for your workforce's hard work.

Whether you play for twenty minutes or twenty hours, there’s always something new to click, build, or unlock on your glorious paradise.

Animal Mystery: 100 Hidden Cats

Find the Cats Hidden Around the World!

Are you ready to find the cats hidden in the world’s most popular and iconic places? Every scene awaits you in a detailed environment inspired by the real world… but be careful, the cats are cleverly hidden and won’t give themselves away easily!

Game Features:

• Race Against Time — The game is entirely time-based. The faster you find them, the higher you climb. Players who finish in the shortest time earn a place on the world leaderboard.

• Hint System — If a cat is giving you too much trouble, you can press the hint button to reveal its location. But remember, every hint adds extra time to your total score.

• Wrong Click Penalty — Clicking in the wrong place adds a time penalty. And if you keep clicking wrong, the penalty stacks and grows. Being careful is just as important as being fast.

• Achievements — Unlock achievements throughout the game and crown your progress. Speed, precision, and discovery await you.

Ready? Find the cats, manage your time, and put your name on the world leaderboard!

Midnight. More slices of someone else's ordinary life.

From the night you sign the contractor agreement, you are the moderator on the night shift. You sit at the terminal you were issued, review each short video that comes in, and decide: approve, or report. That was supposed to be the whole job.

Some of the videos are not normal.

[The job]

  • Review the night's posts one at a time, in order.

  • Approve if nothing is wrong. Report it if you find an anomaly. Decisions cannot be undone.

  • Missing one is a mistake. So is reporting a clean post — both count the same way.

  • The anomaly doesn't stay inside the video. It reaches the terminal, and it reaches you.

  • The contract runs eight nights. See it through.

[An anomaly can be anywhere on screen]

Most of them are in the video: something crossing behind a window, the shape of a dog, the direction water falls. But on some nights the footage is entirely normal and the anomaly is still there — in the desktop wallpaper, in the shape of a button in the app. Some anomalies exist to make you doubt where you were looking.

[Your predecessor left things on this machine]

The feed is not the whole stage. You are working inside a full desktop environment: messages from the moderator before you that grow stranger as the nights go on, an employee handbook that keeps getting revised, and the intranet portal of YONAKA Inc., the agency that placed you here. Everything you need for the job is probably already on this machine.

[Recommended for]

  • Fans of spot-the-anomaly horror in the vein of "The Exit 8"

  • Players who enjoy psychological tension

  • Anyone looking for a horror experience in short sessions

  • Anyone at home in a short-video feed UI

[Features]

  • Spot-the-anomaly horror relocated to a short-video social feed

  • A convincing app UI inside a fully operable simulated desktop

  • Misses and false reports weigh the same — you cannot report on a hunch

  • An eight-night contract of decisions you can't take back

  • Interface in English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Korean

[Video / Streaming Guidelines]

  • Both individuals and companies may post and stream videos without prior permission.

  • Monetization is permitted only through the features provided by the video platform itself.

  • We'd appreciate it if you credit "Anomagram" in your video title or description and include a link to the store page.

  • We accept no liability for any damages arising from streaming or posting this work.

  • These guidelines are subject to change without notice.

The train should have arrived hours ago. Now you're trapped with something that shouldn't exist.

After a worrying phone call, you rush to board the train—only to find that instead of the usual peaceful journey, subtle hints point to something hidden. Anomaly Express is a first-person co-op horror game where you explore a night train, spot anomalies, and survive deadly encounters.

In the game, you’ll encounter:

  • Single‑player mode and co‑op for up to 4 players

  • Anomaly-hunting gameplay across shifting train compartments

  • Deadly encounters triggered by missed or ignored anomalies

  • Atmospheric environments inspired by liminal spaces

  • Four close friends, each with a unique personality yet bound by unbreakable bonds

  • A charming visual style that invites you deeper into the mystery

Anomaly Grid is a turn-based strategy puzzle game built around numerical pressure, color control, and tactical decisions.

Every unit has a value. Every tile matters. To expand, you must capture weaker tiles, defeat enemy units, merge your own forces, and spend score wisely on upgrades and abilities. The board keeps growing stronger over time, forcing you to plan ahead instead of simply reacting.

Control colors to unlock powerful score milestones, push deeper into enemy territory to improve your long-term economy, and decide when to invest in upgrades or deploy abilities that can shift the entire match.

Abilities allow you to boost captures, grow units over time, drain enemy color groups, pressure all enemy units, or instantly strengthen a key unit. Each choice changes the rhythm of the board.

The enemy is not passive. It upgrades, captures, merges, uses abilities, and adapts through different difficulty levels and AI behavior settings. Optional mutators can dramatically change the rules of a match, creating more aggressive, unstable, or chaotic games.

Key Features:

- Turn-based tactical grid gameplay

- Score-based economy and upgrades

- Color control and milestone bonuses

- Unit capturing, merging, and long-term growth

- Five distinct ability types

- Multiple game modes and difficulty levels

- Optional mutators that alter the match rules

- Clear end-screen statistics showing score, captures, upgrades, abilities, and outcome reason

- A focused demo version built around the core 5v5 experience

Anomaly Grid is designed for players who enjoy strategic planning, puzzle-like positioning, resource management, and watching small numerical decisions grow into massive consequences.

Anomaly Vault is an industrial sci-fi horror simulation in which you become an employee of APC, the last corporation remaining in a dystopian world. Analyze unidentified anomalies, construct automated processing facilities, and survive incidents that spiral beyond control.

You have been assigned as a temporary worker to APC Branch 2-1, an anomaly processing facility. Each day, you must investigate anomalies and install the appropriate conveyor equipment. If every procedure is completed according to protocol, you may make it safely to the end of your shift.

Countless anomalies are stored in capsules within APC’s containment sector, awaiting their turn to be processed. Spheres that pulse with light in the darkness. Minerals that react to physical contact. Entities that lure workers toward them. Every anomaly has different properties and reacts in its own way. Even the same procedure will not always produce the same result.

Observe each subject. Conduct experiments. Record every change in its readings. You must determine the correct processing procedure for yourself.

It is difficult work, but there is no need to be afraid.
Should you fail, APC has no shortage of replacements.

At APC Branch 2-1, every anomaly is classified and managed according to detailed measurements such as temperature, size, weight, energy, and activity state. Once you have identified the necessary processing conditions, it is time to automate the procedure.
Set the direction of the conveyors, install the required equipment, and design a processing line that operates each device in the correct sequence. A variety of conveyor equipment is available for use in your facility.

Transform complicated procedures into the simplest possible flow. Turn repetitive work into an efficient automated system. A properly designed line will transport, process, and dispatch anomalies according to specification—all in your place.

A single mistake can put the entire facility at risk. If an anomaly is processed incorrectly, the facility may suffer a total blackout. Contaminants may engulf the work area. A living entity may break free from its capsule and begin roaming the corridors. Of course, even when an incident occurs, the work must continue.

With only limited information at your disposal, identify the cause, modify your automated line, and confront the threats wandering through the facility yourself.

APC records everything. Observation logs. Recovery reports. Notes left behind by previous workers. Audio recordings that were never deleted.

As you continue your work, you will uncover traces of the strange events concealed within APC Branch 2-1. How far you choose to pursue the truth is up to you. Just remember one thing:

You were not hired to uncover the truth.

Grow from cosmic dust into a galactic singularity

Another Black Hole Incremental is a short-run action incremental about turning every collapse into permanent growth.

You begin as a fragile black hole with only seconds of Stability. Consume dust, asteroids and larger celestial bodies before your time runs out. When collapse becomes inevitable, reform, spend the Radiation you earned, and return stronger.

Short runs. Permanent evolution.

Every run is a race between growth and evaporation. Hunt valuable prey, manage your remaining Stability, use active abilities, and decide whether to push toward one more objective or preserve what you have already earned.

Between runs, invest Radiation in a branching Upgrade Constellation. Improve your survival, gravity, accretion, tidal power, scanners, active abilities and maximum scale. Your choices shape how quickly, safely and efficiently your singularity evolves.

Break cosmic defenses

Larger targets are not simple health bars.

Planets, stars, rival black holes and the Galactic Core use layered defenses, sealed phases and spatial objectives. Strip their outer layers, destroy supporting structures, survive gravitational shockwaves, reposition around active breach sectors and exploit the final collapse window.

Raw power helps you complete each phase faster, but it cannot remove the encounter itself.

Build your singularity

• Survive longer and chain multiple objectives in a single run.

• Specialize in tidal force and exposed-phase destruction.

• Control movement, repulsion and orbiting matter through gravity upgrades.

• Use scanners to locate objectives and anticipate cosmic threats.

• Convert surrounding debris into sustained growth through accretion.

• Unlock and evolve active gravitational abilities.

A focused power build may achieve the fastest campaign, while survival, control and information provide safer and more consistent routes.

Rise through four cosmic scales

Your journey begins as a newly formed singularity and culminates at the center of a galaxy:

• Consume debris and asteroid fields.

• Challenge planets and a gas giant.

• Break through a stellar catastrophe.

• Hunt the Prime Rival and breach the Galactic Core.

Each scale introduces new objectives, threats and opportunities to reshape your build.

Deterministic campaigns and verifiable runs

Every campaign has a shareable seed. Random Campaigns, player-entered Seeded Campaigns and exact Practice Run seeds are tracked separately.

Campaign summaries record your time, route, upgrades, ability usage and run seed, making it possible to replay challenges, compare builds and develop faster routes.

The First Galaxy

The opening chapter tells the story of a tiny black hole becoming powerful enough to consume the Galactic Core.

Collapse. Reform. Evolve. Consume the galaxy.

You are both the historian and the creator in this creative fusion of grand strategy and sandbox map-making. Create a vast, procedurally created planet, add distinct countries to it, and stop time. See how sophisticated societies develop economies, declare wars, put down uprisings, and create royal families on their own and if that doesn’t satisfy you seize control to change the global order to your liking.

Key Features:

Create Your Own World: Create stunning landscapes with oceans, dynamic heights, and a variety of biomes. Dislike a continent? Paint the environment, create new boundaries, and create custom nations with distinct cultures and forms of governance by using the powerful in-game editor.

Self-governing AI :
Each country has its own thoughts. The AI actively recruits standing troops, builds strongholds, assesses diplomatic risks, and manages its budget. Over hundreds of simulated years, watch as violent succession crises, peasant uprisings, and intricate webs of alliances develop completely on their own. Watch as countries grow, budget, and exchange resources in a simulated economy. Observe whether the population increases as a result of good policies or declines as a result of starvation or conflict. AI will never be perfect, but it will always attempt to set up trade agreements, feed its people, and increase its war chest.

Player Interaction:
You have the power to change the world's destiny at any time; you are not merely an observer. Take direct leadership of a kingdom to lead it to worldwide conquest, start catastrophic civil wars in an enormous empire, or bestow a large treasure on a small underdog nation. All nations actions are recorded and is up for review whenever you want either as a timelapse or as a chronicle for each nation.

Whether you're a grand strategy veteran, a tabletop worldbuilder, or simply someone who loves watching a complex simulation run its course, your world is waiting to be written.

FEED NEST. GROW SWARM. DEVOUR WORLD.

Nest almost empty. One ant still moves. Outside waits food, enemies, and strange offerings. Somewhere in dark, something hungry.

Ant Mill Inc is a dark real-time incremental ant colony game. Gather food. Grow nest. Fight enemies. Begin with one ant. Become thousands upon thousands.

COLONY THINKS FOR ITSELF

No controlling ants one by one. You shape the colony. The colony decides the rest.

Each ant sees only nearby things. Food. Danger. Nest. Pheromones. Ants explore, find resources, carry them home, call more ants with trails, and fight whatever gets in way.

Good trail gets stronger when many ants follow. Food gone? Smell fades. Ants find new way. Thousands of tiny minds become one great swarm.

GROW COLONY

Make ants spawn faster. Make ants move quicker, see farther, and carry more. First, few workers. Then, black tide.

SHAPE COLONY

Build vast upgrade tree. Find new resources. Tear down barriers piece by piece. New lands wait beyond.

FIGHT FOR COLONY

Crush hostile creatures. Break rival nests. Kill mighty bosses. Colony fights same way colony lives. More ants. Better ants. No stopping.

SAVE COLONY FROM HUNGER

The great worm never full. Feed it resources, or sacrifice ants at altar for Souls.

Challenge worm when you dare. Come weak, worm eats colony.

WHAT GAME HAS

  • Many ants, each with its own small mind

  • Pheromone trails that grow strong, then fade

  • Vast upgrade tree

  • Creatures to fight

  • Barriers to tear apart piece by piece

  • Strange offerings and powerful artifacts

  • Wildlife, bosses, and rival ant colonies

Kill Your Friend!

Since ancient times, when conflict arose between penguin tribes, each side would send forth their champion warrior to settle matters in one-on-one combat.

What began as a tradition has since become a beloved spectacle that all penguins go wild for.

For glory. For survival. To kill your friend.

Strike down your opponent and claim victory!

Defeat Fuels Your Strength

Don't be too discouraged by a loss. Every defeat is a lesson on the path to victory — grow stronger through upgrades and come back swinging!

Choose from over 90 upgrades and find your own way to win!

Antiques were once known in Chinese as gudong (骨董), a term meaning “odds and ends.” In his Thirteen Discourses on Gudong, Dong Qichang describes disparate objects from antiquity brought together as a category of their own, calling them gudong. Another interpretation gives each character a deeper meaning: gu (骨), “bone,” represents the enduring essence of the past—just as bones remain after flesh decays—while dong (董) means “to understand.” In this reading, gudong means understanding the essence left behind by the ancients.

In Antique Dealer, you can collect a variety of distinctive antique cards and play strategic card matches.

Collect


The game holds 600 antique cards from ten Chinese dynasties, from the Xia to the Ming, each with six quality levels.

Leave the game running and a new card arrives every half hour, quietly keeping you company.

The collection can shrink to a single small card in a corner of your desktop, so it never gets in the way.

Every card you collect goes on display in your Antique Codex, sorted by dynasty and quality, so you can browse it any time.

Combine

Drag a spare card onto another spare card of the same dynasty and quality to combine them.

When combining Quality I–V cards, you can choose a card of the same dynasty one quality level higher as your target, with a chance to receive a higher-quality card from a random dynasty instead.

Quality VI cards let you choose a card of any quality from the same dynasty as your target.

Play

When you want a challenge, play the built-in card game and outplay rival dealers with what you know about the cards and a sound strategy.

The Book of Changes says: "When it is time to stop, stop; when it is time to act, act. When movement and stillness each come at the proper time, the way is bright."

For an antique dealer, timing is everything. The largest collection does not make you the winner, nor does one profitable deal. When the dust settles, the dealer holding the most silver wins.


Every antique card has a dynasty, a quality rating and a hidden truth: genuine or fake.

Some cards give themselves away, because their dynasty, name and picture don't match.

A genuine card can bring handsome profits, and a fake one is not necessarily worthless.

You can swallow the loss, take your chances on a buyer who does not know better, expose a fake to drive down its dynasty's market, or bluff a rival into taking it off your hands.

The choice is yours.


Each dynasty has its own independent market level.

A card's market value depends on its quality and its dynasty's current market level. Sales, showcases and exposed fakes, in turn, can push that level up or down.

When a dynasty's market reaches its ceiling, its market is sealed, and all cards from that dynasty are confiscated. Once three dynasties have been sealed, the game ends immediately.


Each game consists of multiple rounds, up to a maximum of 15.

Every round has five distinct phases.

The Five Phases of a Round


As night falls and old wares fill the stalls, you come here to stock your shop.

Every Hidden Market merchant has a distinct temperament and their own rules.

Some sell everything at half price; others offer that deal only on the second item. Some move stock fast, selling only in bulk; others let you take a close look before you buy. Some find all manner of excuses to charge you extra; others specialize in buying back second-hand cards from one dynasty.

Each game brings a different mix of merchants. Cheap does not always mean a bargain, and expensive does not always mean a trap. Study the wares, the merchants and your rivals' choices before deciding where to spend your silver.


Objects gathered from across the realm by the authorities are up for auction today. With the right connections, your own wares can find their way into the catalog—and you can get an early look at what is waiting in the storeroom.

Before bidding begins, you can pay to inspect lots in private, or slip a card of your own into the sale.

Once the auction opens, dealers take turns bidding or dropping out. The last one standing pays and takes the card.

When you enter your own card, only you know whether you are selling a treasure or setting a trap. (Though, let's be honest: everyone knows it's a trap.)


Put a card you have confirmed as genuine on display for everyone to see: your shop's showpiece.

Your showpiece can change the turn order, and a high-quality card may let you act first in the dealings that follow.

A showpiece also raises the market level for its dynasty. As it takes center stage, the market for that dynasty rises with it.

Your showpiece cannot be sold until you take it off display.

Your showpiece is not there to tempt a buyer, but to make those who know its worth think twice before underestimating you.


Choose cards to put on your stall, pay the stall fee, and wait for customers to come calling.

Better stall positions cost more, but customers see—and buy from—them first.

Foot Traffic determines which cards can sell. If foot traffic is too low, you can also spend silver on a sales pitch to attract buyers with deeper pockets.

Knowledgeable customers can tell genuine from fake. Genuine cards sell at market value, while fakes are exposed, earning you nothing and driving down their dynasty's market level. But if the buyer does not know better, a fake card can sell at market value too.

You can also admit that a card of yours is fake, giving up a potential sale to drive down that dynasty's market.


Cards that fail to sell during the Open Market remain on their stalls.

You can make a take-it-or-leave-it offer for another dealer's unsold card;
or wait a little longer and then pick up cards that still have not sold for half their market value.


With 30 Hidden Market merchants, over 600 antique cards both genuine and fake, shifting foot traffic and market levels, and rival dealers scheming at every turn, each game is full of surprises and the outcome is never certain.

Other dealers will vie with you for auction lots, bid up prices, hide information and manipulate the market. When you are most desperate for silver, they may even take a card off your hands at a price you find hard to refuse.

You might lead from the very first round, then fall behind after buying one fake after another. You might also sit on unsold stock for round after round, then make one decisive sale before the market hits its ceiling and turn the entire game around.


First Steps: Follow a detailed tutorial and learn the rules of the trade as you buy and sell.

Classic Game: Choose your difficulty and test your wits against three other dealers.

Dealer League: Compete in a tournament of a hundred shops, advancing through four-player matches, breaking through round after round to vie for the title of champion.


You and 99 NPC-run shops make up this world of dealers. Every dealer has a history and a reputation, along with distinct trading preferences and abilities. If one of them makes you lose your cool, you can replace that NPC at any time.

Your opponents use underlying strategies or trained reinforcement-learning AI models, weighing potential profits, risks and timing based on the information they have. You will meet shrewd veterans who calculate every move, and rivals whose decisions leave you guessing.

I have one non-negotiable rule for the computer opponents: no cheating. They do not get to see a card's authenticity before the rules allow it. They do not secretly change the odds or conjure extra silver out of thin air. Their calculations and decisions draw only on public information and their own inspection results, under the same rules you play by. They may guess right or wrong. They may set a trap—or fall into yours.

I want the outcome to come down to information, judgment, nerve, calculation and a little luck—not a system quietly taking sides.

Computer opponents can still make poor decisions, and their unconventional moves may leave you scratching your head. That, too, is part of the game.


Disclaimer

The trading scenarios and rules in this game are designed for gameplay and entertainment only. The antique cards are virtual items designed from elements of cultural relics, and the gameplay, items and values shown in the game do not represent anything in the real world. Nothing in the game is real-world advice on antiquities appraisal, trading or investment. Please comply with the laws and regulations applicable to collecting and trading in your jurisdiction.

Ants TD is a chaotic Tower Defense where thousands of ants race for your nest. Build your defenses, dig paths, drop barricades and bait them with fruit to steer the swarm exactly where you want.

Evolving Tower Defense.

  • New enemy nests crack open mid-game and dig fresh paths onto the map forcing you to adapt.

  • Face a variety of challenging enemies, from exploding ants that disable your defenses to flying ants that ignore routes entirely, and eventually even the Ant Queen herself.

Control the flow of ants.

  • Ants always take the fastest route to your nest. You get to decide what that route is.

    • Dig new paths to drag them past all your defenses.

    • Barricades block the shortcuts and encourage ants to take the long way round.

    • Fruit piles lure the swarm into corners it would never willingly visit. 

Push back against the swarm!

  • Face literal thousands of ants at once.

  • Shoot, Explode & Burn as many ants as you can.

  • Unlock epic abilities to keep the swarm at bay.

Craft the ultimate defense

  • 18 units and buildings. Pick 6 to take with you to burn, butcher, and explode the swarm.

  • over 50 unlockable perks & mutations. Take up to 5 with you to create particular advantages and potential new challenges.

A perfect organism

Experiment with DNA to create new, unique species with special abilities and traits. Watch as they change colours and shapes as you progress trough the vastness of space and conquer new territories.

The Invaders

The asteroid-riding termites are back and trying to destroy all the space ants! Join the battle and defend multiple universes in this tiny yet epic adventure! Remember, in the race for survival size doesn’t matter.

This may be a small step for an ant

Navigate the dangerous depths of space and pilot your spacecraft full of ants.

Fly through unknown obstacles in search of valuable resources and the means to ensure your survival.

Think like ant, build like a colony

Explore, collect resources, and uncover secrets on uncharted planets with different biomes. Build ant societies and overcome the challenges of the unknown.

Small moves, massive impact.

Take part in intense, high-stakes battles with dangerous foes at every turn. You must carefully choose when to engage in combat or when to retreat to safety.

Cozy crafting meets chaotic fantasy adventure. Run a blacksmith shop in a fantasy valley, alone or with up to 5 friends. Hammer every tool by hand, sell it to customers, collectors and the occasional thief, then step through the portal for rarer materials. Mine it, forge it, sell it, explore deeper. Repeat.

MINE IT

Swing your pickaxe through copper mines, iron depths, mithril caves and volcanic caverns. Crack rich veins for triple ore and dodge falling rocks and gas vents. Careful: some ore is alive, and it runs.

  • Caves and forests grow back every day, and new ones open as you progress

  • Chop enchanted trees and dig up mushrooms that make you faster, bouncier or stronger

  • Build a mine cart line so ore rolls home on its own

FORGE IT

Every tool is made by hand. Jump on the bellows to keep the furnace hot, hammer the glowing spot on the anvil, or land a Masterstroke that finishes the head in one hit. Press it onto a handle, sharpen the edge and it's ready for the rack.

  • Pickaxes, axes, hammers, shovels and swords, from copper to charged orichalcum

  • Mix alloys like bronze, steel, pewter and orichalcum

MORE THAN METAL

Cut and stitch leather into helmets, pauldrons, shirts and boots. Brew mushroom potions, blow your own glass bottles and pour pewter into molds. Then trace glowing runes on the altar to charge your tools with frost, ember or storm.

SELL IT

Flip the sign, open the doors and watch customers pick your work off the racks. Better and sharper pieces sell for more.

  • Hagglers, collectors, chatterboxes, and picky customers who sigh at your best work

  • Thieves and garden gnomes who grab your stock and run. Your shop dog takes it personally

  • Commissions, market days, knights' tournaments and storms change what sells

  • Expand the shop, sweep the mud and read the day's ledger every evening

EXPLORE DEEPER

The valley gets wilder the further you go: the Frozen Forest, the Fire Forest, volcanic caves and a storm peak where the lightning finds you.

  • Over 15 creatures, from goblin raiders and night trolls to magma golems, a chained demon and a storm elemental

  • Sword combos, armor and potions to survive the cold, the heat and the bite

  • A discovery ledger for every tree, ore, creature and secret you find

BETTER TOGETHER

Play solo offline, or run the shop with up to 6 players online. One friend mines, one forges, one haggles, and somebody always forgets to sweep. Host a public, friends-only or private world, or join with a room code.

REPEAT, BUT BIGGER

Finish milestones to move through six ages: Copper, Iron, Bronze, Steel, Mithril and Orichalcum. Each age unlocks new stations, metals and places to explore, and your humble workshop grows into a thriving business.

FEATURES

  • Hands-on crafting: forging, sharpening, leatherworking, brewing, glassblowing, casting and rune infusion

  • Your own fantasy shop with haggling, commissions, thieves, weather and calendar events

  • Living caves and forests that grow back every day

  • Over 15 creatures, from ore that runs away to a chained demon

  • Six ages of progression and dozens of milestones

  • Solo or online co-op for up to 6 players

  • Over 80 Steam achievements

  • Playable in 14 languages. As a solo developer I used machine translation to make that possible, so some lines may read a little off. Spot one? Let me know and I’ll fix it

Anxiety Mori is a short first-person psychological horror game about a man haunted by his past. After a traumatic event cost him his family, his happiness, and his sense of self, he fled from everything he knew. But running doesn't silence memory. As the past keeps resurfacing in the present, the line between what is real and what is imagined begins to collapse.

What You'll Do
The Present: The Leftover

  • Mop floors and pick up trash to clean up The Leftover

  • Search the messy rooms to find items you need

  • Collect rent money from the residents and deliver it to the apartment owner

The Past: The Memory

  • Run from the people who hurt John and reach the exit before they catch you

  • Fight back against them with a bat when there is no way out

  • Piece together what really happened to him and his family

The Story

The narrative is told out of chronological order. You'll move between the present and fragments of memory, discovering how the two are connected and where they lead. The story deals with trauma, guilt, and anxiety, and is meant to be felt as much as understood.

Key Features:

  • Around 1 hour of playtime: a focused, self-contained horror experience

  • Two timelines: an uneasy present and a terrifying past, played in alternation

  • Told out of chronological order psychological story told through memories, environments, and hallucinations

  • Atmospheric first-person exploration of The Leftover and The Memory Past

  • Cleaning and item-finding gameplay in the present, chase and bat combat in the past

  • Automatic flashlight to light your way through dark areas

  • Blurred reality: you'll often be unsure what is real and what is in his head

  • Keyboard and mouse support

  • Available in English

Content Note

Anything Goes Derby is a party game that mixes horse racing with a classic naming game: take turns naming things that fit a theme.

Give your racehorse any name you like that fits the theme, then send it out to race.

If the theme is "sushi toppings," will your runner be Tuna, Salmon, or the connoisseur's pick, Sea Urchin?

Play solo, take on strangers in Random Match, or get a group together: up to 8 people as horse owners, and up to 64 including spectators.

Speed, Stamina, Power, Guts, and Wits. Running style (Front, Stalker, Closer, or Late), distance aptitude, even coat color. Everything is decided by the name you give it, and the same name always makes the same horse.

Find a name that fits the theme and wins!

Keep your favorite horses in the stable to build up their race records and bring them back for the next race.

Races play out automatically as a 3D simulation, with synthesized-voice commentary that reads the names you chose out loud. (The commentary voice is in Japanese, with English subtitles.)

Switch between multiple camera angles at any time and see how it ends: a wire-to-wire escape, a charge down the far outside, or a head-to-head duel all the way down the stretch.

Can't wait for the result? Skip ahead to the drama of the final turn.

Buy betting tickets from the race card before the off, starting at ¥100 a ticket.

The real deal: 7 bet types (Win, Place, Quinella Place, Quinella, Exacta, Trio, and Trifecta), plus Wheel, Box, and Formation bets.

Pick your betting style: Easy for quick bets, or Detailed for building your own combinations.

Back your own horse, or jump ship to someone else's that looks like a winner.

If you go broke, you'll be topped back up to ¥1,000, so don't worry about blowing your whole bankroll!

Compete with every player on the Steam rankings for the highest odds hit and for daily and weekly betting profit.

All money is in-game currency only. It can't be bought with real money or cashed out.

Spend your winnings on a gacha to collect horse skins. From real tack like ear bonnets and leg bandages to crowns, UFOs, jetpacks, and even dragon wings, mix and match over 250 items by body part and make your horse impossible to miss!

Horse skins have no effect on race results.

Full Version Bonus: Buy the full version by November 30, 2026 (JST) to get the exclusive horse skins Ink Wash, Ink Brush, and Ink Splatter.

Up to 8 players meet online, each bringing up to 4 horses into the same race.

In a Private Match, spectator mode lets up to 64 people play at once!

"Wait, does that name even fit the theme?" Call a vote. If the majority agrees, that horse is scratched.

Send reactions during the race, and give carrots to the horse you're rooting for. The owner of the horse with the most carrots wins the Carrot Prize.

  • 302 themes (food, animals, places, characters, and more). The host can also set any theme they like

  • 4 distances (1200m / 1600m / 2000m / 2400m), turf and dirt, left- and right-handed courses, 3 weather types, and 4 track conditions. Change the conditions, and the "strong names" change too

  • 7 bet types, 250+ horse skins, and 44 reactions

  • The host can freely set race conditions, field size, and the time limit for each phase

Play any character, in any world*

Anywhere RPG is a real-time, top-down 2D sandbox RPG where an AI director acts as your personal game master. You don't pick from a menu of actions. You type whatever you want to do, like "pickpocket the merchant," "convince the guard I'm the king's cousin," or "attack the bandit." The AI decides whether it's plausible, rolls the dice, narrates what happens and changes the world to match. Nothing is scripted. Everything is generated and resolved live as you play.

Describe any setting, such as a medieval village, a haunted space station or a noir detective city, and the game builds an explorable world around it. You get regions, buildings, items, quests, and NPCs with their own personalities and daily routines.

  • Emergent gameplay: AI-run events, quests that adapt to what you do, and survival stats that fit your setting.

  • Progression: skills generated for your world, perk trees, active abilities and hotkeyed free-text macros.

  • Play your way: endless sandbox, pause anytime, god-mode editor, and every AI prompt is moddable.

No subscription required

The base game includes a default AI service and is fully playable with no setup and no extra cost. You get unlimited turns (slower after very heavy use, affecting less than 5% of players), and about 2 new worlds or 20-50 new locations per day.

An optional monthly subscription adds more daily world/location generations; a larger AI memory; better text, image, and speech models; and more monthly full-speed turns.
